source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across two buildings and 175,000 square feet of technical space, and its certifications point at regulated enterprise workloads rather than AI training.

The campus ranks sixth among the nineteen Texas facilities that publish power capacity, which is 6.9% of the state's disclosed total of 475 MW. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, so that rank measures how many operators disclose, not how much capacity the state holds. The 33 MW is a specification, not a measurement of load.

The certifications are HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type 2, TIA-942 and HITRUST. They qualify the campus for healthcare, federal and payment workloads, which are compliance requirements rather than AI-specific markers. Nothing published states accelerator count or rack density, so any conversion from megawatts to GPUs rests on an assumed 40 kW per rack and eight accelerators per rack, roughly 825 racks and 6,600 accelerator slots. That is arithmetic, not disclosure.

What the data does not cover is the part that would matter for AI scaling. There is no grid interconnection, no power source, no statement of whether the 33 MW is contracted, allocated or available, and no breakdown of demand by workload. The suitability score of 68 is built from published IT capacity and operator type alone, and it lists announced expansion as missing. A reader can see that a regulated enterprise campus of this size exists in San Antonio. A reader cannot see whether it trains models.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
